aboutHtml:
Data sources

Kanji list and JLPT levels: kanji-data by David Gouveia (MIT License). Levels are based on Jonathan Waller's JLPT lists. The JLPT has not published an official kanji list since 2010, so levels are a guide only.
github.com/davidluzgouveia/kanji-data · tanos.co.uk/jlpt

Readings, English kanji meanings and radicals: KANJIDIC2, Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group (EDRDG), CC BY-SA 4.0.
edrdg.org – KANJIDIC

Example words, readings and English meanings: JMdict, EDRDG, CC BY-SA 4.0 (via the jmdict-simplified JSON release by scriptin).
edrdg.org – JMdict · github.com/scriptin/jmdict-simplified

Writing practice (stroke order and shapes): KanjiVG by Ulrich Apel, CC BY-SA 3.0.
kanjivg.tagaini.net

Turkish meanings and radical names: Written for this project and shared under CC BY-SA 4.0 as derived data.

Fonts

Noto Serif JP, Zen Kaku Gothic New and Manrope; SIL Open Font License 1.1 (Google Fonts).

Licence

The dictionary data in this app is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0: you may use and adapt it with attribution, and must share adaptations under the same licence.

This application uses the JMdict/EDICT and KANJIDIC dictionary files. These files are the property of the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, and are used in conformance with the Group's licence (edrdg.org/edrdg/licence.html).

The message is sent straight to the developer with your phone's e-mail app and goes nowhere else. The “⚑ Report a mistake” link on grammar, conversation and word screens fills in this form for you.

restoreHelp:
Merge: progress from this device and the backup is combined and nothing is deleted. Favorites and notes are combined; for reviews and writing the more advanced record is kept; this device's settings stay the same.
Replace: this device's progress is deleted and replaced by the backup.
